items.recommendation: Upgrade CL: Understand → Apply. DS=3 stays (DCS default for Apply). ExplanationCorrect references COSO Principle 17 by name — EV3 passed.

reclassification_recommendations.rationale: Detailed operative scenario (19/200 items failed, $18,500 variance vs $15,000 threshold, 23 unexamined variances). Candidate must parse specific facts and apply COSO Principle 17 to determine the correct audit response. This is Apply, not Understand. DS stays at 3 (DCS default for Apply).

Operative scenario ('400,000 wire transfers monthly', 'treasury operations center', 'risk assessment framework'). Candidate must apply inherent-risk concepts to a specific banking scenario. DS stays at 3.

Specific fraud scenario ('never ordered and never received'). Candidate must diagnose which control mechanism (three-way match) would have prevented this specific fraud pattern. Requires application of control knowledge to fact pattern — not mere concept recognition.

All three are cosmetic company-name wrappers on 'X is reviewing internal controls.' Removing company name leaves equivalent concept-recognition question. CL should be Understand per ALIGNMENT_MAINTENANCE_GUIDE §2.2 scenario-operativity test. DS=1/Easy is justified at Understand level because distractors include obviously-wrong options (capital budgeting, wait for external audit).

These have genuine operative facts requiring application. CL=Apply is correct. But DS=1 is 2 levels below DCS default of 3. Upgrading to DS=2 (Moderate-Easy) with -1 modifier justified by single-step reasoning and company-name-only scenario format. P1-E-044 (bank reconciliation control purpose), P1-E-048 (perpetual inventory), P1-E-052 (lockbox system).

P1-E-056 ('A warehouse manager who has custody of inventory is also assigned to perform the annual physical inventory count') is an independent topic (physical count control independence), not a DL-012 clone. DL-033 entry flags it as 'Independent topic, possibly mis-archived'. Should be reviewed and re-certified. ExplanationWrong fields are short (1-2 sentences) — borderline for DL-025/026 but not empty. Would benefit from explanation expansion during re-certification.

cross_reference_pack_e_section_e.consistency_analysis: MAJOR_DISPARITY. Pack E Section E is 74/75 Understand (98.7%) with pure definition-matching stems ('The control environment reflects:', 'Risk assessment involves:', 'Control activities include:'). Pack A Section E is 46/58 Understand (79.3%) with 12/58 Apply (20.7%) and scenario-based stems. Both are Section E (Internal Controls) but were authored through completely different pipelines. Pack E Section E tested definition recognition; Pack A Section E tested concept application in business scenarios. Difficulty also diverges: Pack E has 33/75 Moderate items (44%) at Understand level — these are DCS-inflated. Pack A has 3/58 Moderate (5.2%) at Understand level — more realistic.
cross_reference_pack_e_section_e.pack_e_dls_issue: 33 Pack E Section E items at Understand/Moderate (DS=3): DCS default for Understand is Moderate-Easy/2. These items are pure definitions at inflated difficulty. This is the Pack E difficulty inflation pattern documented in S719 Agent C Block-C. 24 of these items were moved from Difficult→Moderate by S719 but are still 1 level above DCS default.
cross_reference_pack_e_section_e.recommendation: Pack E Section E 33 items at Understand/Moderate should be downgraded to Moderate-Easy/2. Pack A Section E has the more accurate Section E calibration. Recommend using Pack A Section E as the cross-pack reference standard for Internal Controls domain difficulty calibration.
